answers.answer: Select 3 randomly chosen Escape Pod tokens for 4 players. Place the lowest-numbered Pod in section A and the next in B, alternating A/B in numerical order; all start Locked-side up. The Intruder bag starts with 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player (so 7 Adults at four players).

Remove all Personal and Corporate Objectives marked for a player count above the actual count; shuffle each deck separately and deal each player 1 of each before Character drafting. The first time any Intruder miniature appears, each player immediately chooses one of their two Objectives and removes the rejected one face down from game, unseen. Eggs do not trigger this choice.

Discard the used Action card itself plus exactly 2 additional Action cards as its printed cost. Contamination cards can never pay an Action cost. If the card has sections separated by “OR,” choose one effect.
answers.evidence: Actions — Action Cost; Actions from Action cards

answers.answer: They take 1 Light Wound only after finishing their own round in the burning Room, including the round in which they pass. Having used one Action means they must pass, and passing ends their normal Actions for this Player Phase; passing also allows discarding any number of hand cards. They do not burn again in later players’ rounds that turn; fire damage applies at the end of their own round only.

On entering the empty unexplored Room, rotate the tile so the Exploration-token number faces the Item Counter symbol, resolve its effect, then remove the token to the box. Afterward, because the Room is empty, roll Noise. On a Silence result there is no Noise marker, unless the Character has Slime, in which case resolve Danger. Danger skips the Noise roll: all eligible neighboring Intruders (not in Combat) move into the Room; if none are eligible, put Noise in each connected Corridor without a marker. If a Character or Intruder was already in the destination Room, no Noise roll is made at all.
answers.evidence: Movement, Rooms and Corridors; Exploration tokens; Noise roll

answers.answer: Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards, follows ordinary Movement restrictions and replaces the post-move Noise roll by placing a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the destination Room. It is forbidden in Combat and when every Corridor connected to the destination already has Noise. A Closed Door blocks crossing; a Character may never stop in a Corridor.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions — Careful Movement; Movement, Rooms and Corridors

answers.answer: Because the rolled number points to a Corridor that already has Noise, resolve an Encounter instead of placing another marker. Clear every Noise marker in all Corridors connected to the Room first, including the Technical Corridors space if its Entrance connects there. Draw one token and place its matching Intruder miniature in the Room; compare the token number with the triggering player’s hand size, counting Action and Contamination cards. Fewer cards than the number causes a Surprise Attack against that triggering Character. If the token is Blank, instead put Noise in every connected Corridor, return Blank to the bag, and add an Adult if it was the last token and one is available. A Technical Corridors Entrance makes its space connected. Set the drawn non-Blank token aside outside the bag until a rule returns it.
answers.evidence: Technical Corridors; Encounters; Blank token in an Encounter

answers.answer: Danger moves every neighboring Intruder that is not in Combat with any Character into the destination. If there are none eligible (including if all are in Combat), place Noise in every connected Corridor that lacks it; count Technical Corridors when the Room has an Entrance. An Intruder moving into a Character’s Room is not an Encounter, though they are then in Combat. Slime changes every Silence result (Noise roll or Exploration) into Danger.

During an Encounter, clear all connected Noise first. If the drawn token is Blank, place Noise in every Corridor connected to the Room; return the Blank to the bag, and if it was the last token in the bag add 1 Adult token if available (otherwise none). No miniature appears and no Surprise Attack comparison is made. In bag development, Blank instead adds 1 Adult token if any are available, then Blank returns to the bag.
answers.evidence: Blank token in an Encounter; Intruder bag development

answers.answer: Both Intruders stay in their starting Room; together they destroy the Closed Door token, which becomes a lying Destroyed Door. Destroyed Doors allow movement and cannot be Closed again, except with Plasma Torch. If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to appear through a Corridor with a Closed Door, the Door does not block appearance.

On movement into a Technical Corridors Entrance, the Intruder miniature is removed, its Injury markers discarded, and its token returned to the bag. A Noise marker already on the Technical Corridors space remains. Characters cannot use Technical Corridors except via Mechanic’s Technical Corridors Action card or Technical Corridor Plans Item; Doors can never be placed there.

Shoot costs 1 Action card and 1 Ammo from a Weapon in Hand and targets one Intruder in your Room; the target must be Intruder type and is subject to die-symbol target restrictions. It does not require or draw Contamination. On a miss, nothing happens to the target; a double-hit result gives 2 Injuries before Weapon modifiers. Melee costs 1 Action card, draws a Contamination card onto your Action discard pile, targets an Intruder in your Room and rolls the Combat die; a miss inflicts 1 Serious Wound on you, and double-hit counts as only 1 Injury.

After adding Injury markers, check the Intruder’s Injury Effect using its current total Injuries. Larva dies at 1 Injury. Adult checks 1 Attack card’s blood value; blood value no greater than total Injuries kills it. Queen checks 2 cards and sums blood; sum no greater than Injuries kills. On death remove the miniature and place an Intruder Carcass in the Room for Adult and Queen (Larva has no Carcass). If any drawn Queen check card has Retreat arrow, retreat occurs instead of a numerical death result: move it via the Corridor number on a drawn Event card, then discard that Event card.
answers.evidence: Intruder Injuries and death; Intruder Retreat

answers.answer: Escape is a Movement Action costing 1. Before moving, resolve one Intruder Attack for each Intruder in the starting Room, ordered larger to smaller: Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva. The Escapee is targeted. If they die, their Corpse stays in the Room they tried to leave. If they survive, complete movement to the neighboring explored or unexplored Room; resolve Exploration if needed and Noise if the destination is empty.

With several Characters, an attacking Intruder targets the one whose player holds the fewest Action cards; ties go to the Character with First Player token, or next in turn order. A non-Larva draws one Intruder Attack card: matching attacker symbol means resolve its effect, otherwise miss; ignore blood value. Larva draws no Attack card: remove the miniature from the board, place it on target’s Character board and give target 1 Contamination card. If target already has a Larva, attacking Larva disappears, existing Larva remains, and target still gets a Contamination card; this does not automatically kill them.

No: dressing flips a Serious Wound face down and ignores its effect, but it still counts toward the 3-wound limit, so any further Wound kills at three Serious Wounds. A third Light Wound clears the Light Wound track and gives a Serious Wound. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound as specified by the healing effect. On death, put a Character Corpse token in the Room and drop all Heavy Objects there.

Canteen/Shower can scan all Contamination cards in your HAND only, removing each scanned non-Infected card from game. An Infected result with no Larva before the scan keeps the infected card and places a Larva; if a Larva was already present, the Character dies and a Creeper appears in the Room. Canteen also heals 1 Light Wound; Shower also removes Slime. Surgery scans all Contamination in deck, hand and discard, removes all Infected cards and a Larva if present, then inflicts 1 Light Wound and automatically passes; all cards, including hand and remaining Contamination, are shuffled into the Action deck, leaving hand empty until next turn. Surgery does not give a new Contamination card.
answers.evidence: Contamination scan table; Player Reference — Canteen, Shower, Surgery

answers.answer: In a Room with uncarried Eggs, Shoot or Melee targets them; each Injury destroys one Egg. A missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound; successful Egg Melee Contamination treatment is unresolved in the summary. A Grenade destroys 2 Eggs; Molotov destroys 1, thrown at a Room with Eggs as if an Intruder were there. After every individual attempt to destroy an Egg, roll Noise. Fire destroys 1 uncarried Egg per Fire Damage step (2 with Vulnerability to Fire). The rules do not specify that the Intruder-target melee penalties apply to Eggs; missed Egg Melee explicitly waives its normal Contamination/Wound.
answers.evidence: Eggs and the Nest; Vulnerability to Fire

answers.answer: To enter, pay 2 Action cards for the matching Evacuation Section Room Action, where a Pod must be Unlocked and have space; no Intruder or Malfunction may be in the Section. Roll Noise first; if an Intruder appears or is already in the Section, entry fails. Each Pod holds 2 Characters and Heavy Objects use no Character space. After boarding, you may launch immediately, removing Pod and passengers’ miniatures from the game; they count as arriving on Earth but still face Contamination and Objective checks. Or wait: pass this turn, remaining present in the Section for bag-development Noise rolls. At the start of each later Player Phase’s first round, choose exactly one: wait and pass, launch, or exit free into the Section Room and take a full 2-Action round. A second boarder may launch the waiting Pod with both aboard. An Intruder appearing in the Section returns all Pod occupants to its Room. A Malfunction while waiting still permits wait, launch or exit; it blocks only new entry.

Victory checks resolve Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, Objectives. Reveal Engines: 2 or 3 Damaged makes ship explode and everyone aboard die; launched Pod passengers are away. If ship survives, reveal Coordinates and read the entry indicated by Destination marker: a non-Earth destination kills hibernating Characters, but not the ship or Intruders; Quarantine Objective sleeper survives if destination is Mars. Then every survivor including Pod passengers has Contamination check: if no Larva, scan all cards in Action deck, hand and discard; if none Infected, skip four-card draw. If any Infected or a Larva, shuffle all Action and Contamination cards from those zones and draw top 4; any Contamination among four kills, otherwise survives. Non-Infected cards are not removed by this end check. Finally check Objectives. Pod passengers do not escape the Contamination check.

Shuffle all Room tiles “2” unseen and randomly put one face down on each “2” slot, returning extras unseen; do the same with all “1” tiles. Shuffle Exploration tokens unseen, place one face down on each Room tile and return extras. Put one random Coordinates card face down by Cockpit; place Destination marker at B. For each of 3 Engines, shuffle its Working and Damaged tokens face down and stack on matching slot; top indicates true status. Place 5 Eggs and 3 random face-down Weakness cards on Intruder board. Time marker starts on green Time Track space. Destination starts B; the summary does not specify a fixed Coordinates card/destination result beyond random card and B marker.
answers.evidence: Setup — board steps 2–13; Player Reference key numbers

answers.answer: Deal numbered Help cards to assign Player Numbers, setting choice order. Deal Objectives before Character draft. Shuffle Character draft cards; Player 1 draws 2, reveals both publicly, keeps 1 and shuffles other back; proceed in Player Number order. Each gets Character board, miniature in colored ring starting in Hibernatorium, shuffled 10-card Action deck, Starting Weapon in a Hand slot loaded to its Ammo capacity, and two horizontal inactive Quest Items. First Player token begins with Player 1. Blue Character Corpse begins in Hibernatorium. Quest Items are not active at start; fulfill their printed mini-quest to flip to normal usable Items.

At start of every Player Phase, each player draws from Action deck to 5 cards (or 6 through Cabins). If drawing while the Action deck is empty, shuffle that Character’s discard pile into a new deck, then draw. After drawing, pass First Player token left except on game’s first turn. Normal used/discarded Action cards go face up to that Character’s Action discard pile; gained Contamination cards go on top of it and are never costs. Normal discards are face up, but an explicit effect may set another destination.

Event Phase: advance Time (and Self-Destruct if active); Intruders in Combat attack; each Intruder in a burning Room takes 1 Injury and immediately resolves its usual Injury Effect; resolve Event card, first movement then event effect; then bag development. Event-card movement applies to each Intruder of the card’s symbol that is not in a Room with any Characters; move it through the Corridor numbered on card. A Technical Corridor destination removes miniature and returns token to bag. Discard Event after effect unless card says otherwise; if Event deck empties shuffle discards into a new deck. Intruder Attack deck when empty is reshuffled from its discard pile.

Bag development: Larva is removed from bag and 1 Adult added. Creeper is removed and 1 Breeder added. Adult returns immediately before all players roll Noise in order (skip Combat); an Encounter during rolls may draw that same Adult. Breeder causes Noise rolls in order, skipping Combat, then Breeder returns. Queen: if any Character is in Nest, place Queen and resolve Encounter; otherwise add 1 Egg to board (also if Nest undiscovered), then return Queen token. Blank adds 1 Adult if available and returns Blank. Discarded/dead Intruder tokens return to reusable token pool; tokens withdrawn for development return/are removed as specified. Rolls happen for all players per effect, and next turn begins only after full development and resulting Encounters/Surprise Attacks resolve.

If instructed to place a ninth Fire marker, ship explodes; a ninth Malfunction makes ship lose hull integrity and game ends. Max 1 marker per Room; extra placement where that Room already has the marker does nothing. Removed markers return to their marker pool. When hull integrity is lost, all Characters aboard including sleepers die, and all other things aboard including Intruders die.
answers.evidence: End of the game; Fire and Malfunction markers

answers.answer: A Malfunction disables that Room’s Action and Computer; Search remains usable. Repair effects can discard it. It cannot be placed in the Nest, Room Covered in Slime, or an unexplored Room. It does not change an Engine token’s status; Engine Room status is unaffected though its Room Action is disabled. Malfunction in Hibernatorium does not affect already hibernating Characters.

Normal Item cards are hidden in Inventory holders; other players see card backs/colors. No Inventory size limit. Show any Item card when using it. Heavy Items and Objects are visible and occupy one of 2 Hand slots. Heavy Items cannot exceed 2 slots; Duct Tape combines 2 Heavy Items into one slot, never Objects. Add Items attach to another card and act as one; adding Extended Magazine/Auto Loader to an empty or used Energy Weapon grants extra Ammo immediately. Searching weapons come with 1 Ammo and never exceed printed capacity. The summary does not identify which further “added Items” beyond Add-type rules, so further specifics are unsupported.

Drop is free at any time during your turn, with no Action: dropped Objects remain in Room; dropped Items are lost/discarded. Found Weapons from Search come with 1 Ammo; Starting Weapons are loaded to their own printed capacity at setup.

Search chooses deck matching Room color: Red, Yellow or Green; in white Room, choose any of those three. Draw 2 cards from one deck, keep 1 and put rejected one face down on bottom of that same deck. Each Search lowers Room Item Counter by 1; at zero it is emptied and cannot be searched, except Scout Scavenging. Nest and Room Covered With Slime prohibit any Search Action. Blue Crafted Items are never found by searching. The summary’s Storage Room Action has its separate rule and works at zero counter.

Craft Item Basic Action costs 1 Action card and discards 2 Item cards whose blue Component icons match the two gray icons on a Crafted Item card. The result card must be available; otherwise cannot build it. You may inspect the Craft deck at any time. Crafted Items and component symbols: Antidote flame + medical cross; Taser battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool; Flamethrower flame + screwdriver/tool; Molotov flame + folded cloth/fabric.

Only the Trade initiator pays 1 Action card; all Characters in the Room may join and exchanges occur only if parties agree. You may give Items/Objects for nothing; Characters cannot exchange Ammo. Searching Heavy Items do not require a separate Pick Up Action; the Pick Up Action applies to Heavy Objects.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions — Trade and Pick Up Heavy Object; FAQ Actions 1–2

answers.answer: Discover weakness by researching matching Object (Character Corpse, Intruder Carcass or Egg) in Laboratory using Analyse; object must be present in Laboratory. Corresponding Weakness card is revealed face up and remains on Intruder board, not consumed; its rule benefits everyone. Anyone may do the research, and Discover Weakness Objective does not require you personally to research.
answers.evidence: Objective types; Player Reference — Laboratory; FAQ Intranet research

answers.answer: Most Room Actions cost 2 Action cards, require being in Room, and are forbidden in Combat or a Room with Malfunction. Computer icon itself has no effect specified in summary; Malfunction makes the Room’s Computer unavailable. Fire does not prevent Room Actions or Searching; Characters suffer a Light Wound only if they end their own round in the burning Room.
Armory adds 2 Ammo to one of your Energy Weapons only, not Classic Weapons, and cannot raise it above printed Ammo capacity.

Emergency Room has three mutually exclusive choices: dress all Serious Wounds; heal 1 Dressed Serious Wound; or heal all Light Wounds. Dressing turns each Serious Wound card face down so its effect is ignored but the Wound remains and counts toward three. Duplicate Serious Wound effects do not stack, though duplicates make them harder to get rid of.
answers.evidence: Character Wounds and death; Player Reference — Emergency Room

answers.answer: Comms Room Action “Send a Signal” places a Status marker on your Character board’s Signal space, used only for Objectives. A Comms Room is always aboard.
answers.evidence: Player Reference — Comms Room; Objective types

answers.answer: Fire Control chooses any one Room, discards its Fire marker if present, then all Intruders there run away in random directions (draw one Event card per Intruder to determine movement). It works even if Room has no Fire, to scatter Intruders.

In Generator Room, start by placing Status marker on first green Self-Destruct space; stop by removing it. A new sequence restarted begins at green. It advances one space whenever Time advances. At first yellow it cannot be stopped and all Pods unlock automatically; they may later be relocked, and subsequent yellow spaces do not unlock them again. Reaching final skull space explodes ship. If a hyperspace jump occurs while active, ship is still considered destroyed. Character cannot start it while anyone hibernates; Coolant Leak Event can. Once anyone hibernates, Character cannot initiate it.

Airlock Control targets any one other Yellow Room, only if all Corridors connected to it have no Destroyed Doors. Immediately close every Door around it and place Airlock Procedure token. If every Door remains Closed at end of current Player Phase (when all pass), everything in Room dies and any Fire marker is removed. Opening any Door first cancels procedure.
At start of a new turn, Character in Cabins with no Intruders present draws 1 extra Action card for a 6-card hand. Malfunction disables it. It is passive, not a paid Room Action.

Command Center can select any one Room and Open or Close any of its connected Corridor Doors, choosing individually which Doors; summary does not list exception for Destroyed Door, but Destroyed Doors can never be Closed again except with Plasma Torch. Thus it cannot close Destroyed Door.
answers.evidence: Player Reference — Command Center; Door tokens

answers.answer: Engine Control Room checks status of all 3 Engines, even if an Engine Room has Malfunction; cannot change status there. Malfunctions in Engine Rooms do not affect this check.

Hatch Control System flips one Escape Pod token to Locked or Unlocked. Monitoring Room secretly looks at one unexplored Room tile and its Exploration token, then replaces them; user may lie about what was seen. It does not inspect explored Rooms per its stated scope.
answers.evidence: Player Reference — Hatch Control System; Monitoring Room

answers.answer: Entering Room Covered With Slime automatically gives Slime marker; no separate Action. No Item count is set there and Malfunction cannot be placed there. Slime maximum is one; further does nothing. Shower removes Slime but does not remove Fire; Fire can exist in Shower Room and showering does not extinguish it.
answers.evidence: Player Reference — Room Covered With Slime and Shower Room; Slime marker

answers.answer: In Cockpit, Check Coordinates secretly looks at Coordinates card and may lie; replace it and remember it. Set Destination moves Destination marker. Marker selects one of four destination entries on Coordinates card. Cannot set Destination if Intruder is in Cockpit or change it once anyone hibernates. Summary says information secrecy (may lie) but not who else can see an action; check is described as secretly looking. Cockpit is a Special Room, and not searchable.

In Engine Room, Check Engine secretly looks at top token; may lie. Repair/Break via Repairs Action or Tools Item secretly examine both tokens and restack in any order; need not say whether repaired, but must say if order changed. No prior check or functioning Engine Control Room required; works despite a Room Malfunction.

Hibernation allowed only when Time marker is on blue space, in Hibernatorium with no Intruder or Malfunction, paying 2 Action cards. Roll Noise; Intruder appearing/reaching Room makes attempt fail; otherwise remove miniature and stop participating until end checks. Once anyone hibernates, no Character can change Destination or initiate Self-Destruct. A later Hibernatorium Malfunction does not wake or harm sleepers; ship destruction and endgame checks can still kill them.

When Time reaches final red, ship jumps immediately; awake Characters on board die from g-force while hibernating spared; Intruders unharmed. Last alive non-hibernating Character on board dies, hibernates or launches: if Self-Destruct active move its marker to final red and resolve destruction, otherwise move Time to final red and resolve. If Self-Destruct is active at jump, ship still considered destroyed. Normal jump does not kill Intruders.
answers.evidence: End of the game; Self-Destruct sequence

answers.answer: No, Characters cannot directly attack one another due to anti-aggression implants. Indirect harm is possible: lock someone in a burning Room, activate Self-Destruct with crew aboard, or throw Grenade into Room with other crew.

If Adult must be placed but all 8 models are on board, Adults not in Combat retreat: remove all such Adult models and return their tokens to bag if possible, then place an Adult in Encounter Room. If all eight in Combat, summary says its source does not explain how to provide model and authoritative clarification is needed. Intruder ending movement in unexplored Room does not reveal Room or Exploration token and is not removed.
answers.evidence: Adult overflow; Intruders in unexplored Rooms

answers.answer: Small curled symbol hits Larva/Creeper only; against Adult, Breeder or Queen it is a miss. Larger curved symbol hits Larva/Creeper/Adult; against Breeder/Queen miss. Shoot miss does nothing. In Melee, same target restrictions; an ineligible symbol is a miss and inflicts 1 Serious Wound on Character.

No Larva and all cards scan non-Infected means no four-card draw; scanned cards are not removed at end check. Pod passengers still undergo final Contamination and Objective checks, so earlier launch does not bypass Objective.

Antidote = flame + medical cross; Taser = battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool; Flamethrower = flame + screwdriver/tool; Molotov Cocktail = flame + folded cloth/fabric. These are icon components shown on Items, not inferred Item card names.

In Combat whenever an Intruder occupies your Room; Eggs do not count. Actions marked In Combat Only or Out of Combat Only are limited accordingly. Unmarked card and Item Actions are usable in either situation, subject to their requirements. Basic Actions in Combat are limited to Shoot, Melee, and Basic Movement as Escape; no Trade, Craft, Pick Up Heavy Object or Quest Item activation. Room Actions forbidden in Combat.
answers.evidence: Actions — In Combat / Out of Combat

answers.answer: Objective saying Player X cannot survive requires that Character dead at game end; you need not personally kill them. Hibernating or escaping means they survive and does not satisfy. “Only survivor” means no other Character may survive. Regardless of Objective, your own Character must survive by pod evacuation or hibernation.

If Door pool empty, move any Door token from elsewhere on board. Open has no token; Closed is a standing token; Destroyed is a lying token. Max one Door token per Corridor; Doors cannot be placed in Technical Corridors.

First Character death automatically unlocks every Escape Pod (flip tokens). For rest of game they may be locked or unlocked normally, e.g. by Hatch Control. The summary flags whether later deaths re-unlock pods after they were re-locked as unresolved: manual says “first” death in one place, “any” death in another.

Storage Room Action draws 2 cards from a chosen Red/Yellow/Green Item deck, keeps 1, puts rejected card face down at bottom of that same deck. It may be used repeatedly even at Item Counter zero; counter limits Search Action card only. Common Room Action costs 2 Action cards and requires presence, no Combat, no Room Malfunction.
answers.evidence: Player Reference — Storage; FAQ Storage; Room Actions

answers.answer: In Nest, take 1 Egg token from Intruder board using Nest Room Action, costing the usual 2 Action cards, then roll Noise. This takes it from board, removing Nest Egg total. Picking up an already dropped Egg token in your Room is Basic Pick Up Heavy Object, costs 1 Action card and has no Noise instruction; dropped Egg is ordinary object and does not restore Nest Egg total if returned to Nest Room.
answers.evidence: Player Reference — Nest; Basic Actions; FAQ Eggs

answers.answer: After showing and using a One Use Only Item Action, discard the Item card.

A Character in a launched Escape Pod counts as having arrived on Earth. This only states the Character’s arrival; ship’s destination is independently determined by Coordinates and is not established as Earth.
Yes. While waiting in a Pod, you remain treated as present in the Section for Noise rolls from bag development.

A Malfunction appearing in Section while already waiting does not prevent waiting, launching, or exiting; it blocks new entry to Pods only. Thus your waiting occupant may still choose each allowed option.
answers.evidence: Escape Pods — Malfunction while you wait

answers.answer: One separate Intruder Attack per Intruder in Room, before movement, in size order largest to smallest: Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva.
Yes. Remove an Event that says remove itself even when its other effect cannot resolve.
answers.evidence: FAQ — Rounds, events, damage and Intruders

answers.answer: In bag development, return Adult token to bag immediately before all players roll Noise in order, skipping those in Combat. During triggered Encounter, the token may be drawn again.
Ordinarily a retreating Intruder meeting Closed Door destroys it and stays in its Room. Under The Way of Moving Weakness, affected Intruder other than Breeder or Queen instead does nothing at Door.
No. The summary explicitly says the Hand Serious Wound does not increase the cost of Basic Shoot. It does not give a fuller explanation beyond identifying Basic Shoot as a Basic Action.
Vulnerability to Fire adds 1 Injury per damage instance (x+1), not for each individual Injury. Flamethrower double-crosshair result deals 3 Injuries total.
Attacking Larva is removed from board and does not replace the existing Larva. Existing Larva remains; target gains 1 Contamination card. This attack does not automatically kill them.
Sleeper takes no later Fire wounds in Hibernatorium. Ship destruction and endgame survival checks still matter and can kill them.
Yes. Coolant Leak Event can start Self-Destruct even while someone hibernates; unlike Character starting it, which is forbidden when anyone hibernates.
Discarded/dead Intruder tokens return to unused token pool and remain reusable; they are not permanently removed.
Fire can be placed in unexplored Rooms; Malfunction cannot be placed there.
answers.evidence: Fire and Malfunction markers; FAQ Rules 22

answers.answer: The first extra Light Wound (third total) clears Light Wound track and causes 1 Serious Wound; the fourth Light Wound then remains as 1 Light Wound. Final state: 1 Serious Wound and 1 Light Wound.
answers.evidence: Character Wounds and death; FAQ Rules 23

answers.answer: On standard-play death, Heavy Objects drop in Room; Item cards disappear from the game.
No. Pods unlock automatically on first yellow space, can be re-Locked; later yellow spaces do not unlock again.
Ship destruction fulfills kill-Queen and destroy-Nest requirements. But Character must still survive and fulfill their Objective; destruction alone does not make them winner.

No: empty Actions with no meaningful game-state change, including starting Trade with no intention to exchange, should be disallowed. Honest negotiations may end without trade. Any Characters in Room may trade with each other, including non-initiators, while initiator pays.
Quest activation is a Basic Action printed on its card. It is forbidden in Combat but allowed in a Room with Malfunction.

Basic Actions in Combat: Shoot, Melee and Basic Movement as Escape only. Trade, Craft, Pick Up Heavy Object and Quest Item activation are prohibited; Room Actions also forbidden. Unmarked card or Item Actions may still be used if their own requirements allow; marked In/Out of Combat restrictions apply.
answers.evidence: Actions — In Combat / Out of Combat; FAQ Actions 3–5

answers.answer: Yes, Soldier may use Covering Fire for themselves alone. If moving two Characters, each chooses their direction; then make one Noise roll. Any Encounter compares Surprise against Soldier.
Full Auto removes all Ammo and performs one Shoot Action; total damage equals result of Shoot plus half the discarded Ammo rounded down plus Assault Rifle’s +1 bonus.

May see Intruder Attack card before deciding to use Nerves of Steel. It can protect Soldier if another Character triggered a Surprise Attack, but only Soldier benefits; other Characters still suffer their applicable effect (e.g. Frenzy).

Careful Movement replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration result with chosen Noise placement. Reconnaissance also cancels automatic Silence/Danger result. Thus the ability’s movement handling applies rather than automatic token effect.

Captain cannot use Order while personally in Combat. Intercom can make someone else Move out of Combat, applying normal Escape rules. (Intercom permits remote effects under its Action, but target’s Move is still subject to Escape.)
With active Intercom, Motivation affects all Characters in Rooms with a Computer as well as all Characters in Captain’s Room.
Technical Corridors or Technical Corridor Plans entry ignores a Door Exploration token because the entry Corridor cannot be determined; no Door is placed.

No. Interruption requires being in the same Room as Character performing interrupted Action, so cannot Interrupt remote Order by Intercom from elsewhere. Passing does not bar Interruption; official FAQ permits Interruption after passing.
No. Empty hand after two Actions does not automatically make you pass; wait for next round to pass. That extra round may cause another Fire or Bleeding effect.
No. If no Larva before Rest, any number of infected cards detected causes just one Larva, not death. Rest can be fatal if a Larva was already on board before the Action.
Roll Noise in your own Room, not the Nest, when throwing Grenade/Molotov at Eggs in Nest from neighboring Room.
No. Intranet research requires the Object itself to be in Laboratory, regardless of Scientist’s location; carrying it outside Lab cannot reveal Weakness.

Yes, Storage Room Action can be repeated at zero Item Counter, paying normal cost and meeting normal Room Action restrictions. Ordinary Search Action is limited by counter: each Search lowers it by one; at zero Room emptied and cannot be searched, except Scout Scavenging.
With Vulnerability to Fire, each Fire Damage step destroys 2 Eggs in Nest (rather than normal 1).
No. An Egg token taken from board and later dropped in Nest Room is ordinary Heavy Object and does not restore Nest’s Egg total/hit points.
The affected player chooses one Action card from their hand and discards it to their own Action discard pile.
Yes, Medkit and Bandages may be used on other Characters.
No direct recharge: trade the Energy Charge to the other Character; they use it in their own round to recharge their own Weapon.
No Larva is placed. Alcohol’s Infected scan instead gives you a new Contamination card.
Yes. Attaching Extended Magazine or Auto Loader to used or empty Energy Weapon immediately grants extra Ammo.
Crafted Flamethrower starts fully loaded, rather than with the one Ammo of a searched Weapon.

Antidote scans all your Contamination cards across hand, Action deck and discard; removes all Infected cards from game; gives 1 new Contamination card; then reshuffles that card with non-Infected scanned Contamination and Action cards, except cards retained in hand. You may keep hand cards, then pass. Surgery instead scans all zones including hand and shuffles the entire hand too; removes infected cards and a Larva if present, gives no new Contamination, then costs 1 Light Wound and automatically passes with hand empty until next turn.
